Keywords: HTTPException raise status_code detail message headers custom error
Description: Raise HTTPException directly inside route handlers for expected HTTP client errors. Include a descriptive detail string. Pass headers dict for auth challenges (WWW-Authenticate).
When to Use: When a specific business rule is violated: resource not found permission denied input conflict
Anti-Pattern: Returning 200 responses with an 'error' key — misleads clients that check HTTP status codes

Keywords: exception_handler app.exception_handler custom exception class UnicornException JSONResponse
Description: Register app-level handlers with @app.exception_handler(ExcClass) to catch custom exception types globally and return structured JSON. Avoids sprinkling try/except in every route.
When to Use: For any custom exception class that should produce a structured HTTP error response app-wide
Anti-Pattern: Using try/except inside every route handler — boilerplate and inconsistent error responses

Keywords: RequestValidationError override 422 pydantic validation error custom format exc.errors exc.body
Description: Override FastAPI's built-in 422 handler for RequestValidationError to change the error format. Access exc.errors() for the list of validation problems and exc.body for the raw input.
When to Use: When clients need a different validation error shape than FastAPI's default 422 JSON
Anti-Pattern: Returning validation errors as 200 OK responses — misleads HTTP clients and monitoring tools

Keywords: override HTTPException handler starlette.responses JSONResponse http_exception_handler reuse
Description: Override the default HTTPException handler globally. You can reuse FastAPI's built-in handler inside your override using fastapi.exception_handlers.http_exception_handler.
When to Use: When you want to add extra logic (logging metrics) on every HTTPException but keep the default format
Code Example:
"from fastapi import Request, HTTPException
from fastapi.exception_handlers import http_exception_handler

@app.exception_handler(HTTPException)
async def custom_http_exception_handler(request: Request, exc: HTTPException):
    # Add logging or metrics here
    import logging
    logging.warning(f'HTTPException {exc.status_code}: {exc.detail}')
    # Re-use FastAPI's default handler for the response
    return await http_exception_handler(request, exc)"
Anti-Pattern: Duplicating the default JSON response format manually — use http_exception_handler to delegate

Keywords: RequestValidationError exc.body raw body validation debug logging inspect input
Description: Access exc.body inside a RequestValidationError handler to log or return the raw request body that caused the validation failure. Useful for debugging malformed inputs in production.
When to Use: When you need to inspect or log what the client actually sent when validation fails
Code Example:
"@app.exception_handler(RequestValidationError)
async def validation_handler(request: Request, exc: RequestValidationError):
    import logging
    logging.warning(f'Validation error body: {exc.body}')
    return JSONResponse(
        status_code=422,
        content={'detail': exc.errors(), 'body': exc.body},
    )"
Anti-Pattern: Logging full request bodies at ERROR level in production — may log PII. Log at DEBUG or scrub sensitive fields

Keywords: error response model Pydantic responses dict 404 422 OpenAPI docs additional responses
Description: Define a Pydantic model for your error response body and reference it in the endpoint responses dict. This makes error shapes appear in OpenAPI / Swagger docs for client SDK generation.
When to Use: When you want OpenAPI docs to document the shape of error responses
Anti-Pattern: Only documenting 200 responses — leaves clients guessing at error shapes and breaks SDK generation

Keywords: IntegrityError unique constraint 409 conflict SQLAlchemy asyncpg rollback duplicate
Description: Catch SQLAlchemy IntegrityError (unique constraint violations) inside route handlers and raise 409 Conflict so clients know the resource already exists.
When to Use: When creating resources that must be unique (email username slug)
Code Example:
"from sqlalchemy.exc import IntegrityError

@router.post('/', response_model=UserResponse, status_code=201)
async def create_user(body: UserCreate, db: DbSession):
    try:
        user = User(**body.model_dump())
        db.add(user)
        await db.commit()
        await db.refresh(user)
        return user
    except IntegrityError:
        await db.rollback()
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_409_CONFLICT,
            detail='A user with that email already exists.',
        )"
Anti-Pattern: Returning 500 for unique constraint violations — misleads clients into believing it is a server bug

Keywords: catch all Exception 500 internal server error guard production JSON safe fallback
Description: Add a catch-all exception handler for all unhandled Exception types. Returns a safe generic 500 JSON response and logs the traceback. Prevents raw Python tracebacks from reaching clients.
When to Use: In production to prevent internal implementation details leaking in 500 error responses
Anti-Pattern: Allowing unhandled exceptions to return raw HTML tracebacks — leaks implementation details and opens security risks
